figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biochemical characterization of AprY. (A) Proposed reaction pathway; (B) in vitro assays with different divalent metals. Total ion
chromatograms (TIC) are shown. The reactions were performed at room temperature for an hour in 50 μL 100 mM MOPS (pH 7.0) with 10 μM
enzyme, 200 μM 1, 5 mM sodium ascorbate, 10 μM metal and 200 μM NADPH; (C) in vitro assays of AprY and AprR. For the stepwise reactions,
1 was reacted with AprY for an hour. AprR and NADPH were added to the reaction mixture for another hour; (D) AprY requires ascorbate and O2;
and (E) time course analysis of AprY with 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Proposed mechanism of AprY-catalyzed cyclization and biosynthetic pathway of asperipin-2a (2). The Cα ketone oxygen atom at Phe1 in
7 derived from H2O is shown in blue. The acidic proton at Cβ of 7 that is exchangeable with D2O is labeled in orange.
